title: ESA's Juice spacecraft completes Earth flyby
excerpt: The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer used Earth's gravity to increase its velocity by 3.5 km/s.
bodyHtml:
The European Space Agency reported that its Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer, known as Juice, performed a gravity assist flyby of Earth on 28 September. The spacecraft passed 8640 km above the Indian Ocean at 13:45 CEST, utilizing the planet's gravity to adjust its trajectory toward Jupiter.

According to the European Space Agency, the maneuver deflected the spacecraft by an angle of 20° and increased its velocity by 3.5 km/s. The flyby also allowed for the calibration of the spacecraft's 10 science instruments while it traveled through Earth's magnetotail.

Juice is scheduled to return for a third flyby of Earth in January 2029 to set its final course for a 2031 arrival at Jupiter.
topic: Successful Earth flyby improves Juice’s course to Jupiter
